thread.title: Apple: The Standard In A Technological Revolution Has Become Too Cheap - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: Steven Fiorillo
title: Apple: The Standard In A Technological Revolution Has Become Too Cheap - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
I think it is fair to say that Apple ( AAPL ) has earned the right to be called “The Standard” when discussing technology products. AAPL laid the foundation then created the blueprint for everyone else to follow. Recently Apple’s chart looks as if it stepped off of a cliff which makes right now such an amazing opportunity to pick up shares at a deep discount. How many times have we heard Jim Cramer say own Apple don’t Trade it? I really wish investors would follow his advice and view Apple as an investment due to the power of its brand and ecosystem not its short-term financial results as Warren Buffett does. AAPL hit a high of $233.47 in October and in almost three months has fallen to $150.73. AAPL has lost over $82.74 per share since their highs which is just over a 35% reduction. I currently do not own Apple and I am viewing this as a great opportunity to start a position as in my opinion the shares are at least 35% undervalued.
(Source: Inkbot Design )
Apple’s new nickname should be “The Standard” because they created the blueprints and published the playbook for others to follow Since 2001 Apple has been the most innovative product company in the world. I am branding them as “The Standard” because ever since 2001 the measuring stick got a whole lot bigger and never stopped growing. Pre-2001 I don’t consider APPL to be that exciting as they were simply a troubled computer company with minimal market share. 2001 was a tremendous year for Apple as their first retail stores launched and were followed up by the iPod. The Apple Store changed retail in technology and the iPod decimated an entire industry of Walkmans and Discmans. There are defiantly people who will read this article and have no clue what either of those products are thanks to Apple. In 2003 the iTunes Store launched and single-handedly put music stores such as Tower Records out of business. AAPL changed the entire industry of how music is purchased, stored and listened to through the combination of their iPod and iTunes Store. In 2007 Apple enhanced their position in mobile electronics by launching their iPhone which has become iconic and their flagship product to date. In 2008 Apple pioneered a brand-new industry with the launch of their App Store for the iPhone. Their innovation didn’t stop there as 2010 was the year of the iPad which changed personal computing as people didn’t need a clunky computer to enjoy their media or the internet. Most recently in 2015 Apple dropped the Apple Watch which has become a solidified itself as part of everyday life and not just a trend. In addition to all these products Apple still makes some of the best computers you can purchase.
AAPL should be acknowledged as the standard because everything they create is copied by their competition right down to their packaging. AAPL was the first to package their products in a sleek organized box without wasting space. I remember the first iPod I purchased, and it felt like you were opening a real high-end product as everything inside the box was organized with no wasted space. Think about when you purchase products from other companies packaging and branding has become a focal point thanks to Apple. Apple also does everything with purpose and for a reason. They have the best product ecosystem in the world. Every product works with each other from their computers to their mobile devices right down to the Apple Watch. Warren Buffett who has one of the greatest investing minds in history said one of the most brilliant thinks about Apple “I do not focus on the sales in the next quarter or the next year. I focus on the hundred’s, hundreds, hundreds of millions of people who practically live their lives by it [iPhone].”
(Source: Office Timeline )
Think about how many companies have replicated what Apple has done to create success for themselves.
A look inside some of Apple’s very impressive numbers Over the past three years AAPL has sequentially increased their Net Sales and Net Income as their innovation of current and new products & services has fueled their continuous growth. Their net sales for their fiscal year of 2018 came in at $265.5 billion while their Net income came in at $59.5 billion. Over the past three years their Net sales increased by just about $50 billion while net income increased by almost $14 billion. Think about this from the close of fiscal year 2017 to 2018 Apple’s revenue grew by $36.4 billion which is equivalent of a Fortune 100 company in a single year.
(Source: Steven Fiorillo) (Data Source: Apple 2018 10-K )
One of the other items I look for when looking over the statement of operations is if the cash generated by operating activities is increasing as well as the cash and cash equivalents at the on the books at the end of the year. Apple increased the cash generated by operating activities from the end of their 2017 fiscal year to the close of the 2018 fiscal year by just over $11 billion. They also increased their cash and cash equivalents at the end of the fiscal year by over $5 billion over the same period.
(Source: Steven Fiorillo) (Data Source: Apple 2018 10-K)
The beautiful thing about revenue is that it can be generated from more than one business segment. I personally thought it was absolutely ridiculous when the analysts made such a big deal about the number of units which Apple would report in the future. Not every business segment can grow every quarter indefinably. I agree with Apple’s decision to stop reporting units sold. Investors and analysts should care about revenue generated and if revenue is increasing as this is the component which earnings is derived from. Revenue can’t be manufactured by fancy accounting. When looking at 2017 Q4 and 2018 Q4 I love what I see as the year over year change came in at 20% as the total revenue for Apple increased just over $10 billion. As long as Apple is growing their revenue does it really matter on a quarter by quarter basis how many units they are selling? I care about the overall numbers, and if Services outpaces iPhones for a period of time such that they flip flop, I don’t really care as long as the company's overall revenue continuously grows.
(Source: Steven Fiorillo) (Data Source: Apple 2018 10-K)
Apple has entered oversold territory So let me get this straight: AAPL is below where they started for the year yet their revenue increased by $36.4 billion year over year and we're going into the holiday season where they are estimated to shatter earnings. Last year Apple estimated $3.86 per share in earnings for Q4 and came in at $3.89. Apple is predicting they will come in at $4.68 per share in this upcoming Q4. They have beat the past four quarters so I would say the chances of a beat are very good. Even if Apple was to miss by $0.30 per share they would still shatter earnings and grow year over year by a respectable amount.
According to the RSI, AAPL has entered oversold territory. At the beginning of February AAPL entered oversold territory as it declined from $179.10 on Jan 17 th to $155.15 on February 8 th . Since October we have seen AAPL take an even more drastic decline from $233.47 in October to $150.73. This decline has taken AAPL into oversold territory and we are in the midst of their strongest quarter as the holiday season is upon us.
(Source: TD Ameritrade)
Share Buybacks Apple still has $70 billion left in their 2018 share buyback program. At a share price of $165 Apple can buyback over 424 million shares. In addition to the cash on Apple’s books they have $170 billion in marketable securities so it isn’t crazy to think that Apple will announce another $100 billion worth of share buybacks for 2019 especially with the share price at such a deep discount to the recent highs in October.
(Source: Philip Elmer-DeWitt )
Dividends Apple currently has an annualized payout of $2.92 per share which is a current forward yield of 1.94%. This is safely covered by the extremely low 24.8% payout ratio. Apple started paying a dividend in August of 2012 and has increased their annual dividend for the past five years. The quarterly dividend started at $.09 per share and currently sits at $0.73 per quarter. Apples most recent dividend increase was by 15.9% from $0.63 to $0.73 on a quarterly basis. With Apple’s commitment to rewarding shareholders through share repurchasing and dividend increases it isn’t crazy to think they will maintain their large dividend increases from their large profits and cash within their war chest.
(Source: Dividend.com)
Warren Buffett’s holdings through Berkshire Hathaway Warren Buffett is one of the greatest investors of our time and when he speaks everyone should listen. CNBC created the Warren Buffett Archive to celebrate a collection of his works from annual meetings to CNBC interviews and everything in-between. On Monday February 26 th 2018 Mr. Buffett gave an interview on Squawk Box and said “If you look at our holdings, you would assume that we like them in the order in which they rank by dollar value of holdings, but if you look at them in terms of recent purchases over the last year we’ve bought more Apple than anything else.” On August 30 th , 2018 Mr. Buffett gave another interview where he explained that Apple makes their products indispensable. In this interview Mr. Buffett said the iPhone is “enormously underpriced” and that it’s worth far more than the $1,000 Apple charges.” He backed this comment up with the following statement “I have a plane that costs me a lot, a million dollars a year or something of the sort. If I used the iPhone -- I use an iPad a lot -- if I used the iPhone like all my friends do, I would rather give up the plane.”
The Oracle of Omaha Mr. Warren Buffett started a position in Apple through Berkshire Hathaway in the 13F filing published on 5/16/2016. They started the position with just over 9.8 million shares. In less than three years their position has increased to just over 252.4 million shares. The current share price of Apple is lower than Berkshire's average filing price in the last five 13F filings. It doesn’t seem as if Warren Buffett has any worries about Apple and the next 13F filing which should come out on 2/14/2019 should show another increase of Apple shares if were are going by history. I would also be surprised if he didn’t add to his position at these prices.

Three future Catalysts to help increase Apple’s growth could come in the form of 5G, Apple Services and an increasing population
A Bloomberg report reiterated rumors of Apple’s 5G phone would arrive in 2020. 5G will start rolling out in December 2018 and will be in at least 19 cities by the middle of 2019. Even if their competitors release a 5G phone by the middle of 2019 Apple’s brand loyalty is so strong that I don’t see many people switching.
The analyst firm Jefferies said on 10/29/18 that Apple was a buy and put a price target of $265 on the stock. Their analyst Timothy O’Shea thinks that Apple Services could make up 25% of Apple’s revenue by fiscal year 2020 and 40% of their gross profit. This would be led by the App Store and Apple Music. Mr. O’Shea stated that “applying a higher multiple compared to the lower margin hardware business, we see a significant opportunity for investors as Services alone could be worth $111 to $177 per share by that time.”
The third catalyst I would take into consideration is that by 2040 , the global population is expected to grow by an additional 1.8 billion individuals to 9.2 billion people from the current level of 7.4 billion. The global GDP is also expected to double in this timeframe and the per capita GDP is projected to increase. The middle class will expand globally and is expected to grow by approximately 80% by 2030 to reach more than 5 billion people. The total US population is projected to reach 334.5 million by 2020, 347.34 million by 2025 and 380.22 million by 2040.
If you put these three catalysts together, Apple should see continued growth from the upgrade cycle with their 5G iPhones and iPads. If the projections from Mr. O’Shea are even close to being accurate, then a large portion of the current share price would be made up from just the service business which has been growing as Apple puts a strong emphasis on this business segment. The last catalyst which I think goes overlooked is the growing global population and the amount of people joining the middle class. It would take a catastrophe for the global or US population to reverse going forward. While this could happen, I think the more likely scenario is that the population will continue to grow, increasing Apple’s potential consumer base.
(Source: Statista )
Apple has risks which should be evaluated before an investment On December 10 th , 2019 Citi cut Apple’s price target from $240 to $200 based on China concerns. The Chinese exposure represents about 18% of Apple’s total sales so if a ban or additional tariffs were to happen due to the never-ending trade war Apple could be significantly affected. Morgan Stanley also cut Apple’s price target from $253 to $236 due to the situation with China and longer replacement cycles.
Apple also faces economic factors and increased competition. If we head into a recession Apple products are luxury items which will be the first to be cut. Maybe not iPhones but spending additional money on services, iPads or Macs is a real possibility. Many other companies have studied the playbook Apple has written and is doing a great job copying them.
Conclusion I recently became a huge fan of Apple products after my wife gave me my first iPhone for Christmas in 2016. I have since then purchased an iPad mini and an iPad Pro. Apple makes amazing products and I am not sure anyone can take that away from them. The Apple store is consistently the only store that is packed when I go to the mall and their customer loyalty is second to none. I have multiple co-workers and friends who will wake up early to order the newest Apple products at launch.
At $150 a share, Apple looks very cheap to me. We're going into the holiday season which is Apple's best quarter and I have a feeling they are going to knock it out of the park this year. Apple also has a huge war chest which will be returned to shareholders through share buybacks and an increasing dividend. I am planning on starting a position in Apple and will make my first purchase with 50% of the allocated funds. I will either average down if the downward trend continues or average up on our way to the next earnings call. Apple in my opinion is "The Standard" for technology products and this is why their competitors always try to take a page out of their playbook.
Disclosure: I/we have no positions in any stocks mentioned, and no plans to initiate any positions within the next 72 hours.
